title: Pull-to-Refresh Design Principles
summary: This reel outlines six key principles for designing a high-quality pull-to-refresh interaction, focusing on physics, feedback, and responsiveness. It emphasizes creating a sense of weight and continuity to make the UI feel polished and intuitive.

transcript.text: Pull down, let go too soon, nothing loads.
Refresh fires past a threshold, never before it.
Release above the line and the list snaps back, no reload.
Drag further and the pull should resist, like the content carries real weight.
A one-to-one drag feels cheap, weight sells it.
At the threshold, your stretch indicator hands off to a spinner. The gesture becomes the loader itself.
One short haptic tick at the threshold arms the thumb before the finger even lifts off the glass. The hand knows it caught. Feedback beats the release.
Pull past the threshold and the rubber band overshoots, then settles back into place. A hard stop feels broken.
Don't lock the scroll while the reload runs. Keep the list alive underneath. Frozen content feels dead.
Pull is a promise. Go to designmotionhq.com for more. Link in bio.

SCROLL ALIVE: Never freeze the list.
before_after: Compares 'cheap' 1:1 movement vs 'weighted' elastic movement, 'hard stop' vs 'rubber band' overshoot, and 'frozen' vs 'scroll alive' lists.
